questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 4 of 6 seminars were for exchange students. They were said to be on B1 level, but in reality they were B2-C1. For me that was very good. The last two seminars were for german students, which I felt as the level were more advanced.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Courses for exchange students. It is easier to raise the hand in those classes and talk in the open forum, because no one is from Geramany. In the "real" classes for Germans I felt more shy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was dissapointing to find out that Uni is not hostig any parties or scial events. You have to invend them on your own. Therefore the social stuff is very limited, which makes it hard to make friends with german people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The clubbing scene in Berlin and all kinds of cultural offers. Outdoor cinemas

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Concerts + clubbing + friluftskino

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is hard to make friends with german students, as they already have there friends and are more reservated. I mostly made friends with other exchange students. That was fine, but I didnt speek as much german as i hoped

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the clubbing culture and their opening hours. You dont find this at home

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Prepare yourself to be outreaching when it comes to German friends and relations. It doesnt necessarily comes to you on its own.

Be prepared that you still have to deal with Erasmus-administrative stuff on your exchange and it takes time

Allow yourself to spend money and live a good life while you're on your exchange. You only experience this once :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It takes time to figure out there website

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: You dont work during your exchange. For me, mentally, that was very rewarding and giving. I have been enjoying life without any stress factor. There was time for everything. I will try to take it with me back home, I will try not to work as hard, when i get home. Also I got a lot of inspiration for culture and going out.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I lived far from the city so I have been dealing with a lot of traveling time. But it has been ok.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
